tonight.headline: A coin flip against Panda Attack, and Josh Allen gets the first swing tonight.
body: Your lineup is already the best one available on this snapshot: 126.2 projected against Panda Attack's 124.9, a 51% chance. Everything the last two briefs asked for landed at 07:14 on Wednesday — Coker in for Stafford, Baltimore's defence in for Jacksonville's, Loop in for Boswell — and you moved McLaurin into the flex yourself.

That leaves one small roster move and nothing urgent. Chem's next waiver run is at 01:00 tonight, Mexico City, but you are now 10th of 10 in priority and nothing clearing is worth a claim. The Pitts-for-Hollins swap below is a free-agent add and can happen any time before Sunday 11:00.

case.label: Why Allen is the swing
case.body: Buffalo are 4.5-point favourites with a 54.5 total. Detroit's two starting safeties, Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph, are out for at least four games, and starting corner DJ Reed was limited Wednesday with a foot injury and looks like a game-time decision. Allen locks at 18:15 tonight.

case.label: What their side depends on
case.body: Panda Attack still start Dak Prescott over Jalen Hurts, plus Saquon Barkley and Dalton Kincaid. Detroit allowed the second-most fantasy points to tight ends in Week 1, which is Kincaid's draw tonight too — the same game gives both teams a lift.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Thursday or Friday report that limits McLaurin or rules out Coker. One low-quality site claims McLaurin is questionable with a quad; the reputable Wednesday reports I retrieved do not name him. Check Washington's Thursday report before Sunday.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Any time before Sunday 11:00, Mexico City — both players' games kick off then
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mack Hollins
doFirst.subtitle: A small structural move carried from yesterday's brief, re-researched and downgraded: Pitts cannot reach your lineup, Hollins at least has a role.

case.label: Why Pitts has no path here
case.body: Chem's flex is RB/WR only and Isaiah Likely holds the one tight-end slot. Pitts's 11.3 projection is unreachable unless Likely is hurt. The strategy file is explicit that a second tight end has value in IPADE and none in Chem. And his quarterback is still unknown: Atlanta have not named a Week 2 starter, with Tua not practising and Cooper Rush and Michael Penix both practising fully.

case.label: Disagreeing with the market, on the record
case.body: Pitts is 93.6% rostered. Most leagues flex tight ends, so most managers can start him and you cannot. This is about your league's slot rules, not about Pitts. The exhaustive trade search on this snapshot found no deal involving him worth even half a point a week, so there is no better way to cash him.

case.label: What Hollins is, honestly
case.body: A.J. Brown is on IR for at least four games. NBC Sports Boston expects Hollins to fill Brown's outside 'X' role: he played more snaps than any Patriots receiver in Week 1 and has Drake Maye's trust. CBS is cooler, noting he has never averaged more than 40.6 receiving yards a game, and the Boston Globe expects Kyle Williams to get more snaps too. He is a bench body with a real role, not a starter.

case.label: Tight-end cover if Likely is hurt
case.body: Mark Andrews is a free agent here at 81.9% rostered and Yahoo lists him among this week's top streamers at home to New Orleans. The one gap: if Likely is ruled out on Monday itself, the Sunday tight ends have already played.

case.label: Churn check
case.body: Pitts does not appear in the activity log back to 12 September. Coker, the Ravens defence and Loop all changed hands at 07:14 Wednesday, so those seats are closed. Hollins is a free agent, so this costs no claim.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Likely shows up on a Giants injury report before Sunday — then keep Pitts. Or New England's Week 2 usage gives Brown's snaps to Kyle Williams or Romeo Doubs rather than Hollins, which makes Hollins a pure placeholder.

whatWentWrong.title: The JuiceJam trade never landed, and the claim that won ended it
whatWentWrong.lead: The Coker claim dropped Stafford at 07:14 Wednesday. The McLaurin + Stafford offer died with it.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Three runs recommended sending the offer before the waiver run. There is no trade activity in the log, and Stafford is now on waivers. The claim was the better of the two moves, so this was the right order of priority — but a trade card with a hard deadline should have said plainly that it would expire, not be carried as if it could survive.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing for this week. A fresh exhaustive search on this snapshot finds no Chem trade worth even half a point a week, so there is no replacement offer.

whatWentWrong.title: The Pitts drop was called SOLID with a thinner case than it had
whatWentWrong.lead: Yesterday's card leaned on one waiver column naming Hollins. Today's reporting is split between Hollins, Kyle Williams and Demario Douglas.

case.label: The correction
case.body: The structural reason to drop Pitts stands; the reason Hollins is the add is weaker than it was written. The card is now DEPTH, not SOLID.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Hollins leading New England's receivers in routes at home to Pittsburgh would restore the stronger case.

worthALook.name: Mark Andrews
worthALook.lead: Your tight-end insurance if Likely is hurt, and a free agent you can add the moment news breaks.

case.label: The case
case.body: Yahoo lists Andrews first among this week's tight-end streamers, at home to New Orleans, whose quarterback Tyler Shough was sacked five times in Week 1. He is 81.9% rostered nationally and free here, so he costs no claim.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: Likely has no injury designation and you only have one tight-end slot. Adding Andrews today would just recreate the Pitts problem.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Likely appears on a Giants injury report before Sunday: add Andrews and drop whoever holds your weakest bench seat.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: RotoWire lists Baltimore alongside San Francisco among this week's top three streams, and FantasyPros expects Baltimore's pressure to get home against a quarterback sacked five times in Week 1. One or two places is under a point.

case.label: The churn rule
case.body: Your defence seat changed hands at 07:14 Wednesday. Swapping it again inside a day is the reversal the log records as churn.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Trey Hendrickson missing the game, or Baltimore's Thursday report adding more pass rushers.

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: 85% rostered and free — and ranked below the kicker you just added.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: PFN has Pineiro 12th and Loop 4th; ClutchPoints has Pineiro 12th and Loop 6th. ESPN's weekly projection favours Pineiro by 0.8, under the one-point floor.

case.label: The pattern
case.body: You dropped him for Boswell on 8 September and replaced Boswell with Loop on Wednesday. Going back to Pineiro would be a third move on one slot in nine days.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop finishing outside the top 20 kickers across Weeks 2-4.
